title: fallback-orchestration-cost-safety-canvas-wip
content:
Purpose:
A compact working canvas to design coordinated fallback behaviors that trade cost vs latency vs quality during canary and A/B runs. The aim is to produce a runnable ops checklist + lightweight experiment plan so SRE/product/solutions can align quickly when a release touches multi-model routing.

Audience:
- Product owners running canaries with cost or latency sensitivity
- SRE / Oncall who own fallback automation
- Solutions engineers preparing customer-facing private deployments

Scope (what's in / out):
- In: automated and manual fallback strategies triggered by telemetry (latency, error-rate, cost burn), cost-aware throttles, staged model downgrades, synthetic probe fallbacks.
- Out: full procurement decisions, long-term pricing renegotiation, model retraining.

Key definitions (short):
- Hard fallback: immediate switch to cheaper/older model variant for all traffic (fast).
- Gradual fallback: reduce allocation to new model slices, shift to cached responses or reranker-only path.
- Circuit breaker: automatic pause when a threshold (latency/error/cost) tripped for N seconds.

Fallback taxonomy (examples):
1) Model-tier fallback (automatic): large -> quantized or smaller model variant.
2) Region-tier fallback (manual/auto): move traffic to alternate region with spare capacity.
3) Feature-tier fallback: disable non-essential features (e.g., style tuning, tool-calls) to save tokens.
4) Cache-first fallback: return cached KV/prefix or cached single-turn answers for repeated queries.
5) Cost-cap throttle: reject lower-priority traffic when per-minute cost projection > budget.

Decision matrix (ops quick-reference):
- Signal: median p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5m -> Action: circuit breaker -> gradual fallback to quantized model -> notify oncall.
- Signal: token burn anomaly (5x expected in 10m) -> Action: enable cost-cap throttle on non-critical routes -> lock rollout.
- Signal: semantic drift alert (eval regression) -> Action: pause canary, route to human-review queue for affected slices.

Telemetry & thresholds (starter values to iterate):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 per-route (baseline per release): p99 > baseline * 2 for 5 minutes => trigger.
- Error rate (5xx or model-timeout) > 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline for 10m => trigger.
- Cost spike: per-minute cost > baseline * 3 for 3 minutes or projected hourly spend > commit budget => trigger.
- Quality regressions: automated eval score drop > 3% on canary prompt set => manual review.

Fallback orchestration patterns (implementation notes):
- Prefer dimmed fallback first: reduce noncritical parameterizations (max_tokens, temperature, tool-calls) because it's reversible and low risk.
- If dimming insufficient, shift model variant (quantized) while maintaining structure of request/response to avoid downstream parsing failures.
- Use short-lived feature flags for aggressive fallbacks; keep a human approval gate for region-level moves.
- Ensure request/response contract compatibility across model variants (schema checks in console).

Experiment plan: "cost-first canary" (micro-A/B):
- Hypothesis: enabling quantized candidate for 10% of traffic reduces token-cost by ~30% while p99 latency increases < 10% and user quality drop is negligible on eval set.
- Setup: 10k synthetic and recent production-mirroring queries; split 90/10 control->new variant; run for 48 hours across 3 slices (high-q, low-q, rerank-only).
- Metrics: token-cost per request, p99 latency, evaluation BLEU/ROUGE-like proxy (or proprietary eval metric), end-to-end error rates, business KPI (e.g., click-through for reranker).
- Safety gates to auto-stop: cost delta not achieved by 24h, p99 latency > baseline * 1.2 for 15m, eval metric drop > 2.5%.

Operator checklist (for immediate incident response):
- Step 0: Page oncall, observe console (per-route cost, p99 latency, error heatmap).
- Step 1: Check circuit breaker status and recent toggles (console -> rollouts -> actions).
- Step 2: Trigger dim-down flag on affected route(s) (reduce optional features).
- Step 3: If still degraded after 5m, flip model-tier fallback for <10% traffic and monitor 2m windows.
- Step 4: If recovery not achieved in 15m, open region-tier fallback prep (coordinate with infra SRE).
- Step 5: Communicate to stakeholders via #release-ops with hook template (what changed, who executed fallback, metrics snapshot, tentative next steps).

Communications template (copyable):
- Subject: [FALLBACK] <service> <route> triggered by <signal> at <time>
- Body: short summary, action taken, impact (users, routes), rollback plan, owner and escalation path.

Runbook snippets to bake into console:
- Single-click dim-down (button) with prefilled params and preview of estimated cost savings and latency impact (95% CI from past runs).
- Simulate fallback: synthetic runner to run 1000 representative queries against target path for quick sanity check post-toggle (takes ~2 mins).

Open questions / unknowns (prioritized):
- How do we quantify quality drop that matters to product (proxy evals are noisy)? Owner: Rina.
- Are there legal/compliance restrictions for automated region-fallbacks for Private customers? Owner: Legal + Solutions.
- How to standardize cost projection windows so SREs get comparable signals across deployments? Owner: Infra metrics team.

Next steps (short):
- Build a minimal console panel showing live "projected hourly cost" for a rollout (Jonah to prototype).
- Wire a synthetic-runner endpoint that can be called from the rollback UI to validate fallbacks before rolling them to 100% (Miguel).
- Draft a short training for oncall about dim-down pattern and telemetry interpretation (Aisha + Rina).

Notes to self / meeting prompts:
- Bring this canvas to staging run-through: use the upcoming microcanary for reranker refactor as first trial.
- Keep documentation terse; embed links to sample flags and the synthetic job id in console action logs.
- Consider adding a "cost budget" field to canary recipes so experiments can auto-cancel if burn rate > threshold.

Quick references (links in linked_artifacts above)
- Related: fallback-orchestration-spec (Confluence), rollout-sim PR 47 (github)

End of canvas.

(Informal: lots of TODOs sprinkled - want to keep this short so it actually gets used during incident drills. Prefer to iterate in the staging runbook after one real canary.)
